subject: Literature
title: The Comstock Laws and Victorian Morality
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Comstock Laws and Victorian Morality.

hook.text: Anthony Comstock personally destroyed over fifteen tons of books he deemed obscene in nineteenth-century America.

buildup.text: The 1873 Comstock Laws made it illegal to mail anything 'obscene, lewd, or lascivious,' including medical texts.

discovery.text: The laws banned not just erotica but also information about contraception, anatomy, and women's health.

twist.text: Margaret Sanger was arrested under Comstock Laws simply for mailing pamphlets about birth control to women.

climax.text: The Comstock era showed how moral censorship can silence vital health information alongside genuinely harmful content.

punchline.text: Censoring obscenity became a tool for controlling women's bodies.

quiz.question: What unintended consequence did the Comstock Laws have?
options: They banned vital health information including contraception and anatomy texts
